label: dbt
description: Transforms data in place with versioned SQL models, runs them against a Trino deployed here, and publishes the generated documentation of every model, test and lineage edge.

fields.name: trinoConnection
fields.label: Connect to Trino
fields.help: Pick a running Trino to fill in the host and port below. Anything reachable from this namespace works; a Trino deployed by KDPS appears here automatically.

fields.name: trino.host
fields.label: Trino host
fields.help: Service name of the Trino coordinator, filled in by the picker above.

fields.name: trino.catalog
fields.label: Catalog
fields.help: Catalog the models are built in. An Iceberg catalog lets dbt create and replace tables; a read-only catalog only supports views and tests.

fields.name: trino.schema
fields.label: Schema
fields.help: Schema the models are written to. dbt creates it on the first run if the catalog allows it.

fields.name: trino.threads
fields.label: Parallel model threads
fields.help: How many models dbt builds at once. Raise it for wide dependency graphs, lower it to be gentle on a shared Trino.

fields.name: trino.auth.method
fields.label: Authentication
fields.help: Must match how the selected Trino authenticates. Every mode except None requires HTTPS on the Trino side.

fields.name: trino.auth.user
fields.label: Trino user
fields.help: Identity the transformations run as. Grant it write access on the catalog and schema above.

fields.name: trino.auth.password
fields.label: Password
fields.help: Stored in a Kubernetes Secret, never in a ConfigMap.

fields.name: trino.auth.impersonationUser
fields.label: Run queries as (impersonation)
fields.help: Optional. Runs the queries as this user instead of the account above, so Ranger sees the real owner. Trino must allow that account to impersonate.

fields.name: trino.auth.jwtToken
fields.label: Token
fields.help: Bearer token presented on every query. Use a service token with a long lifetime, since nothing refreshes it between scheduled runs.

fields.name: trino.httpScheme
fields.label: Scheme
fields.help: Only unauthenticated connections choose this: the other modes are always HTTPS.

fields.name: project.git.enabled
fields.label: Pull the project from git
fields.help: ON (recommended): the models live in a repository and every run uses a commit you can point at, which is also what lets an external orchestrator run exactly the same code. OFF: mount the project yourself from an existing volume.

fields.name: project.git.repo
fields.label: Repository URL
fields.help: For example https://gitlab.example.com/data/analytics.git or git@gitlab.example.com:data/analytics.git.

fields.name: project.git.subPath
fields.label: Project directory inside the repository
fields.help: Leave blank when dbt_project.yml is at the root.

fields.name: project.git.secretRef.name
fields.label: Repository credentials Secret
fields.help: Optional, for a private repository. A Secret with a key 'token' for HTTPS, or 'ssh' for an SSH key. Public repositories need nothing.

fields.name: project.existingClaim
fields.label: Existing volume holding the project
fields.help: Name of a PersistentVolumeClaim whose root contains dbt_project.yml.

fields.name: docs.enabled
fields.label: Publish the documentation site
fields.help: Serves the generated documentation: every model, its description, its tests and the lineage between them. Built from the project and the warehouse catalog at pod start.

fields.name: docs.refreshSeconds
fields.label: Rebuild the site every (seconds)
fields.help: 0 builds once at start. Set it to rebuild periodically so a scheduled run's results appear without restarting the pod.

fields.name: ingress.enabled
fields.label: Expose the site
fields.help: Publishes the documentation through an Ingress, or an OpenShift Route when the cluster has them.

fields.name: runner.enabled
fields.label: Run the transformations on a schedule
fields.help: For a cluster with no orchestrator. Leave it off when Airflow drives dbt: the same image and the same profile are used either way, so the two never drift apart.

fields.name: runner.schedule
fields.label: Schedule
fields.help: Cron expression in the cluster's timezone. '0 * * * *' is hourly, '0 2 * * *' is nightly at 02:00.

fields.name: airflow.enabled
fields.label: Publish an Airflow DAG for this release
fields.help: Writes a DAG into a git repository your Airflow already watches, so the transformations can be scheduled and monitored there. The DAG asks Kubernetes to run this release's own job template, so an Airflow run and a scheduled run are the same run. Leave the schedule above off when you use this.

fields.name: airflow.dagRepo
fields.label: DAG repository URL
fields.help: Repository your Airflow syncs its DAGs from. Often the same repository as the dbt project. KDPS reuses the project credentials to push.

fields.name: airflow.dagPath
fields.label: Directory inside the repository
fields.help: Where your Airflow looks for DAG files.

fields.name: airflow.schedule
fields.label: Schedule
fields.help: Cron expression written into the DAG. Leave blank for a DAG that only runs when triggered by hand.

fields.name: airflow.kubeConnectionId
fields.label: Airflow Kubernetes connection
fields.help: Connection id Airflow uses to reach this cluster. Leave blank when Airflow runs inside it and uses its own service account.

fields.name: airflow.runTimeoutMinutes
fields.label: Run timeout (minutes)
fields.help: How long the DAG waits for a run before giving up.

variables._description: Authentication mode as a gate, so the security blocks the chart needs can be switched on without the operator ticking a second box.
variables.name: authMethod

variables._description: Trust bundle the platform injects for this release. dbt talks to Trino over TLS in every authenticated mode, so it mounts the same material the other services get, reading the PEM entry rather than the Java keystore.
variables.name: contextTrustSecret

bindings._description: Kerberos: the chart's security block carries the keytab Secret KDPS issued and the principal, and its entrypoint runs kinit before dbt starts. Switched on by the authentication mode so there is no second toggle to forget.
bindings.name: dbt-kerberos-enable

bindings._description: Any authenticated mode reaches Trino over TLS, so the trust bundle is mounted whenever the operator supplied one.
bindings.name: dbt-truststore-enable
